chunks: Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abū Makhlad al-Sarrāj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
that he ruled concerning a man who called another, “the son of a madman,” and the other said to him, “Rather, you are the son of a madman.”
So he commanded the first to flog his companion twenty lashes and said, “Know that you will be followed with the like of it: twenty.”
Then when he had flogged him, he gave the whipped man the lash, so he flogged him twenty lashes, as a punishment disciplining them both.

key_terms.ابْنَ الْمَجْنُونِ: son of a madman; an insulting expression used in the dispute
key_terms.السَّوْطَ: the whip or lash used for flogging
key_terms.يَجْلِدَ: to flog or lash as punishment

ai.seo_question: What was Imam al-Ṣādiq’s عليه السلام ruling when two men insulted each other by saying “son of a madman”?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling by Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام regarding mutual verbal insult involving attribution to madness. The Imam عليه السلام ordered reciprocal corporal punishment so that both offenders would be disciplined for their exchange. The narration reflects judicial handling of abusive speech and the principle of proportionate disciplinary punishment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5069 - Ja'far ibn Bashir narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-'Ala from Abu Makhlad Al-Sarraj from Abu Abdullah (as):
Imam (as) ruled concerning a man who called another "the son of a madman," and the other replied to him, "Rather, you are the son of a madman."
Imam (as) commanded the first man to flog his companion twenty lashes and said: "Know that you will also be given twenty lashes in return."
After the first man flogged him, the flogged man was given the whip and he flogged the first man twenty lashes as a means of punishment to discipline both of them.
